# Edward Boyle Animation Blog

> > Animation student blog documenting character animation, 3D modeling in Maya, and VFX compositing projects

This is Edward Boyle's animation portfolio and project blog, showcasing work from animation courses including character rigging (Sam Rig), walk cycles, weight exercises, 3D modeling tutorials, and compositing projects. The blog features feedback from instructors Alec, Mike, Conann, and Yuan on various student projects including The Black Dog Analogy mental health short film.

## Key Topics

- Character Animation
- Maya 3D Modeling
- Walk Cycles
- Character Rigging
- Sam Rig
- Weight Exercise
- Compositing
- Animation Workflow
- Storyboarding
- VFX Breakdown
- Student Projects
- The Black Dog Analogy
- Animation Planning
- 3D Animation Techniques

## Portfolio & Showcase

- [Portfolio](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2015/11/12/portfolio): Portfolio showcase featuring Sam Rig animations, walk cycles, and storyboards

## Character Animation & Rigging

- [Rigging Sam](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2015/11/12/rigging-sam): Character rigging process for Sam using lattice deformer and IK leg setup
- [Walk Cycles](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2015/11/12/walk-cycles): Sam rig walk cycle tests using stepped vs spline animation techniques
- [Animating Shot 1](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2015/11/12/animating-shot-1): Animating Sam rig walk cycle in Sorcha's environment with camera movement
- [Weight Exercise Playblasts](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/07/weight-exercise-playblasts): Weight exercise animation playblasts showing body mechanics progression
- [Weight Exercise Research 2 – AnimSchool](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/04/weight-exercise-research-2-animschool): AnimSchool tutorials on weight animation and center of gravity principles
- [Weight Exercise Research 3 – Useful Articles](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/04/weight-exercise-research-3-useful-articles): Research articles on animation timing, weight, and force by Jahirul Amin

## 3D Modeling Tutorials

- [Bookshelf Modelling](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/05/bookshelf-modelling): Maya bookshelf modeling tutorial using NURBS, loft tool, and Bezier curves
- [Phone Modelling](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/06/phone-modelling): 3D phone modeling based on home telephone using layered approach
- [Frame Modelling](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/05/frame-modelling): Picture frame 3D modeling in Maya with vertex merging techniques
- [Treasure Chest Modelling](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/05/treasure-chest-modelling): Beginner 3D treasure chest modeling tutorial with viewport shading
- [UV Layouts](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/07/uv-layouts): UV unwrapping layouts for bookshelf, frame, and other 3D assets

## Compositing & VFX

- [Final Compositing Outcome](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/07/final-compositing-outcome): Final compositing project featuring Lawrence with lighting integration
- [Initial Compositing Ideas](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/04/initial-compositing-ideas): Angel and devil compositing concept using Malcolm and Max character rigs
- [VFX Breakdown Examples](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2016/01/05/vfx-breakdown-examples): Analysis of VFX breakdowns from Jurassic World, Ant-Man, and Ted films

## Student Projects

- [St. Patrick's Mental Health Services – Short Film Competition](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2015/11/12/st-patricks-mental-health-services-short-film-competition): Frame of Mind short film competition submission for mental health services
- [Final Idea](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2015/09/30/final-idea): Light-based prism sculpture project by Niall and Edward Boyle
- [Animatic Feedback with Mike, Conann, Alec and Yuan](https://edwardboyleanimation.wordpress.com/2015/11/12/animatic-feedback-with-mike-conann-alec-and-yuan): Animatic feedback from lecturers on depression narrative and triptych style
